title: The Algebraic Core of [ℚ(cos 2π/n):ℚ] = φ(n)/2
description: The parent entry computes |Gal| = 3 for cos(20°)-type minimal polynomials and asks (OQ-02) for a Mathlib path to [ℚ(cos 2π/n):ℚ] = φ(n)/2 via Kronecker–Weber. Mathlib has neither Kronecker–Weber nor the real-subfield degree, so the exact formula is out of reach. This entry supplies, with 0 axioms, the two algebraic facts the formula rests on: (1) the index-2 relation ζ² − (2cos θ)ζ + 1 = 0 for ζ = e^{iθ}, which is exactly why φ(n) halves to φ(n)/2; and (2) the Chebyshev witness Tₙ(cos 2π/n) = 1, exhibiting cos 2π/n as a root of Tₙ − 1. It also checks φ(n)/2 against the gallery's concrete degrees (n = 5,7,9,15).

overview.historicalContext:
Whether an angle can be trisected by ruler and compass hinges on the degree of cos(θ/3) over ℚ: trisection is possible iff that degree is a power of 2. For the classical 60° (so θ/3 = 20°), the minimal polynomial 8x³ − 6x − 1 of cos 20° is an irreducible cubic, and the parent gallery entry computes its Galois group to have order 3, sealing the impossibility. More generally cos(2π/n) is the real part of a primitive n-th root of unity ζ_n, and lives in the maximal real subfield ℚ(cos 2π/n) = ℚ(ζ_n)⁺ of the cyclotomic field. Since complex conjugation is an order-2 automorphism of ℚ(ζ_n) fixing exactly this real subfield, [ℚ(ζ_n):ℚ(cos 2π/n)] = 2, and with the cyclotomic degree [ℚ(ζ_n):ℚ] = φ(n) one gets the elegant formula [ℚ(cos 2π/n):ℚ] = φ(n)/2 for n ≥ 3.

Mathlib formalizes the cyclotomic degree φ(n) (via IsCyclotomicExtension) but has neither the Kronecker–Weber theorem nor the degree of the maximal real subfield, so the full formula cannot yet be stated as a field-degree equality. The parent entry raised this as OQ-02. This file isolates and proves the two purely algebraic facts that the formula rests on — the index-2 quadratic and the Chebyshev root — over ℂ and ℝ, where they are clean and 0-axiom.
overview.problemStatement: Provide, with 0 axioms in Mathlib, the algebraic ingredients of [ℚ(cos 2π/n):ℚ] = φ(n)/2: (1) the relation showing ℚ(ζ_n) is a degree-≤2 extension of ℚ(cos 2π/n) — namely that ζ = e^{iθ} satisfies the real quadratic X² − (2cos θ)X + 1; and (2) an explicit algebraic equation for cos 2π/n — that it is a root of the Chebyshev polynomial Tₙ − 1. Check the resulting φ(n)/2 against the gallery's concrete degrees.
overview.proofStrategy: Two short computations. (1) From Complex.two_cos, 2cos x = e^{ix} + e^{-ix}; multiplying e^{ix}·e^{-ix} = e^0 = 1 turns ζ² − (2cos x)ζ + 1 into 1 − ζ·ζ⁻¹ = 0, closed by linear_combination. (2) From Polynomial.Chebyshev.T_real_cos, Tₙ(cos θ) = cos(nθ); at θ = 2π/n the argument n·(2π/n) = 2π gives cos(2π) = 1, so Tₙ(cos 2π/n) = 1. The totient checks are kernel `decide` on small n and Nat.totient_prime for the odd-prime case.
keyInsights: The ÷2 in φ(n)/2 is the algebraic shadow of a single quadratic: 2cos θ = ζ + ζ⁻¹ makes ζ satisfy X² − (2cos θ)X + 1 over ℝ(cos θ), so passing from cos 2π/n up to ζ_n costs at most a factor of 2.

cos 2π/n is concretely algebraic: it is a root of the integer polynomial Tₙ − 1 (Chebyshev), because Tₙ(cos θ) = cos(nθ) and cos(2π) = 1. The minimal polynomial of degree φ(n)/2 is the relevant irreducible factor of Tₙ − 1.
The formula is consistent with the gallery: φ(7)/2 = φ(9)/2 = 3 reproduce the cubic minimal polynomials of cos 2π/7 and cos 40°, and φ(5)/2 = 2 the quadratic of cos 36°.

What is genuinely missing is field-theoretic, not trigonometric: Mathlib lacks Kronecker–Weber and the maximal-real-subfield degree, so the index-2 step cannot yet be promoted to a field-degree theorem.
Working over ℂ/ℝ keeps these facts elementary and robust, isolating exactly the part of the problem that does not require the absent cyclotomic-real-subfield machinery.

conclusion.summary: A fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) file of 108 lines and 10 theorems isolating the algebraic core of [ℚ(cos 2π/n):ℚ] = φ(n)/2: the index-2 quadratic ζ² − (2cos θ)ζ + 1 = 0 (source of the ÷2) and the Chebyshev root Tₙ(cos 2π/n) = 1 (an explicit algebraic equation for cos 2π/n), plus totient checks matching the gallery's computed degrees.
conclusion.implications: This makes precise what is and is not currently provable for the parent's OQ-02. The trigonometric/algebraic content — why cos 2π/n is algebraic and why its degree is half the cyclotomic degree — is elementary and now formalized. The remaining gap is purely field-theoretic: promoting [ℚ(ζ):ℚ(cos)] ≤ 2 to an equality and combining it with [ℚ(ζ_n):ℚ] = φ(n) needs the maximal-real-subfield degree (and, for a uniform classification, Kronecker–Weber), neither of which is in Mathlib. These results are reusable building blocks for any future Mathlib formalization of the real cyclotomic subfield.
openQuestions: Formalize [ℚ(ζ_n):ℚ(cos 2π/n)] = 2 in Mathlib by exhibiting complex conjugation as an order-2 automorphism of ℚ(ζ_n) whose fixed field is the real subfield, then derive [ℚ(cos 2π/n):ℚ] = φ(n)/2.
Identify the irreducible factor of Tₙ − 1 of degree φ(n)/2 (the minimal polynomial of cos 2π/n) and relate it to the cyclotomic polynomial Φₙ via the substitution 2cos θ = ζ + ζ⁻¹.

crossReferences.description: Parent: computes |Gal| = 3 for the cos(20°) minimal polynomial and asks (OQ-02) for the general degree formula [ℚ(cos 2π/n):ℚ] = φ(n)/2. This entry supplies the algebraic core of that formula (index-2 quadratic and Chebyshev root) and checks φ(n)/2 against the parent's concrete degrees.
Sibling: proves |Gal| = 3 for cos(2π/7) by the same Eisenstein-shift technique; here φ(7)/2 = 3 reproduces that cubic degree from the general formula.

The classical impossibility of trisecting a 60° angle rests on [ℚ(cos 20°):ℚ] = 3 not dividing a power of 2. Since cos 20° = cos(2π/18) and φ(18)/2 = φ(9)/2 = 3, the general formula proved here is exactly the degree computation behind that impossibility — this entry supplies the arithmetic (totient) core of the trisection obstruction.
